text:
Ryan Leonard reached 100 NHL games in Ottawa this week, and the headlines took stock. RMNB's piece carried Spencer Carbery remembering the start: "Can't forget Ovi taking him out with the boys." The more useful number is what he's doing now. At 21, he has six goals and 12 points in 17 games while playing only 14:12 a night.

The goals are earned. He's generating 1.23 expected goals per 60 (the quality of his own chances), up from 0.87 last season, and his shooting percentage is exactly league average. Nothing here is running hot. He also shoots hard (93 mph, 96th percentile on NHL EDGE) and plays heavy, with 31 hits.

For context: forwards drafted sixth to tenth overall usually score about 0.40 points a game in their first full season. He's at 0.71.

What to watch is the other end. Evolving-Hockey had opponents gaining 0.16 expected goals per 60 with him on the ice last season, bottom 9% of forwards, offset partly by the penalties he draws. If that improves, the minutes should follow. Our projection: about 25 goals.
